study_title: The Cost of Hindsight: Auditing Real-Time Neural Forecasts Before the Outcome
study_question: How different are model-performance conclusions when a real-time forecasting system is evaluated from immutable pre-event records versus reconstructed after outcomes are known?

included_scope: Tracked source code at the baseline Git commit

prospective_evidence_summary.snapshot_count_note: Snapshot count is not the same as unique-game count because multiple pre-kickoff snapshots may exist for one game.

prospective_record_requirements: Immutable snapshot ID, record hash, run ID, and batch hash
Game identity, season, week, teams, and kickoff timestamp
Forecast margin, spread, win probability, and ensemble uncertainty
Input status, feature coverage, warnings, and preserved record payload
Market fields retained separately for Hard Rock and reference-market data
Completed result and derived scoring retained separately from prediction snapshot
analysis_restrictions: Do not retrain, replace, or tune the frozen model during the study.
Do not overwrite prospective records with retrospective reconstructions.
Do not remove poor predictions or partial-input records without reporting them.
Do not treat strength labels as validated cover probabilities.
Do not claim a wagering strategy is profitable from diagnostic ATS or unit fields.
Do not substitute reference-market data for Hard Rock execution data.
next_research_requirement: Build a separate, labeled retrospective-reconstruction dataset and compare it with the immutable prospective records.
